### Frame
Import: `import { Frame } from 'raditz'`

Frame — previews a section inside a bordered, rounded card (matching the original catalog). Sections that paint their own full-bleed background (accent bands, announcement strips) pass a `className` that flattens the frame chrome so it just clips them. All other div attributes (`id`, `data-*`, aria, handlers) spread onto the frame element, so callers can anchor/test/style the section root directly.

Props:
  - maxWidth?: string — Constrain the frame width (rides the `--rdz-frame-maxw` custom property).

Usage:
```tsx
<Frame />
```

### SectionActionButton
Import: `import { SectionActionButton } from 'raditz'`

Renders one {@link SectionAction} as a {@link Button}, forwarding every field. `variant = action.variant ?? defaultVariant`; `size = action.size ?? size`. This is the single path from a `SectionAction` to a rendered `<Button>` — inline sites that used to construct `<Button>` by hand now delegate here so field-forwarding is tested in one place.

Props:
  - action: SectionAction
  - className?: string
  - defaultVariant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "soft" | "outline" | "ghost" | "glass"
  - size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg"

Usage:
```tsx
<SectionActionButton />
```

### SectionActions
Import: `import { SectionActions } from 'raditz'`

Renders a row of CTAs from `actions` as {@link Button}s. Returns `null` when there are no actions, so callers can drop it in unconditionally. `size` sets the default for every button (each action may override via its own `size`). The shared CTA renderer for all content-driven sections.

Props:
  - actions?: SectionAction[] — The CTAs to render.
  - className?: string (default: row sx-row-center) — Class on the wrapping row.
  - size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" — Default size applied to every button (per-action `size` wins).

Usage:
```tsx
<SectionActions />
```

### SectionBg
Import: `import { SectionBg } from 'raditz'`

Templated background fills (all token-driven, so they re-theme).

Props: none

Usage:
```tsx
<SectionBg />
```

### SectionHeader
Import: `import { SectionHeader } from 'raditz'`

Renders the eyebrow + heading block shared across all content sections. Returns `null` when both `eyebrow` and `heading` are absent so callers can drop it in unconditionally. `className` defaults to `'col sx-sec__head'` and carries each section's modifier (e.g. `"col sx-feat__head"`).

Props:
  - align?: "start" | "center" — Center or left-align the eyebrow + heading block. Omit to inherit the section's default look.
  - as?: "h2" | "h3" | "h4" (default: h2) — Heading level for the title, so a page keeps a correct outline. Every section heading defaults to `h2` (sibling of the hero's `h2`; the page/app owns the `h1`), so sections composed on one page share one coherent level. The visual size is fixed by `h-section` regardless of level.
  - className?: string
  - eyebrow?: ReactNode
  - heading?: ReactNode
  - headingClassName?: string — Extra classes on the heading tag itself (e.g. a per-section text-measure or ink class like `"sx-cta__title"`) — layout classes belong on `className`.

Usage:
```tsx
<SectionHeader />
```

### SectionShell
Import: `import { SectionShell } from 'raditz'`

SectionShell — the one home for the section layout boilerplate every section variant used to repeat: the preview Frame + `.s-pad` padding + `.s-wrap` max-width wrapper (where the responsive container-query lives), with an optional SectionBackground. Sections become content + a shell choice instead of re-typing the triple-nested wrapper ~50 times. The root is the Frame: `className`, `id` and any other div attributes (`data-*`, aria, handlers) land there, so every section variant that spreads its rest props into the shell supports anchoring (`id`), testing (`data-testid`) and consumer classes for free.

Props:
  - animate?: boolean | "scroll" | "load" (default: scroll) — Content entrance choreography — the section's content blocks cascade in (staggered) in the app-wide entrance style (`data-reveal`). `'scroll'` (the default, also `true`) reveals on scroll-into-view; `'load'` plays a pure-CSS mount animation at first paint (no observer, no blank flash — use for above-the-fold sections like the hero); `false` is static.
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh" (default: none) — Optional decorative backdrop (composes SectionBackground).
  - frameClassName?: string — The shell's OWN class on the preview Frame (e.g. "nav-frame", "ph--neutral"). Distinct from `className`, which is the consumer's class — both merge onto the Frame root.
  - frameMaxWidth?: string — Constrain the Frame width.
  - image?: string — Image URL backdrop (overrides gradient).
  - nav?: ReactNode — A transparent nav rendered above the content, floating over the shared background (the "hero bleed" effect). Pass a nav with no background.
  - pad?: "default" | "sm" | "none" (default: default) — Section padding.
  - padClassName?: string — Extra classes on the padding element (e.g. a section band background).
  - parallax?: boolean (default: false) — Parallax the backdrop.
  - scrim?: boolean (default: false) — Darken the backdrop (scrim); the surface then scopes content to on-dark.
  - video?: string — Video URL backdrop (overrides image + gradient).
  - wrap?: string — Extra classes on the inner `.s-wrap` (grid + gap, e.g. "sx-g3 sx-gap-5").

Usage:
```tsx
<SectionShell />
```

### TestimonialFigure
Import: `import { TestimonialFigure } from 'raditz'`

The avatar + name/role attribution block every testimonial variant renders (Testimonials A/B, TestimonialCarousel) — extracted here, like {@link SectionActionButton}, because it crosses section families. Accepts the shared `Testimonial` shape structurally (quote is ignored); `name`/`role` are individually optional. `className` carries each variant's wrapper modifier (e.g. `"sx-tst__person"`); `as` lets a `<figure>` caller render a semantic `<figcaption>`; `metaClassName` extends the inner name/role column.

Props:
  - as?: "div" | "figcaption" (default: div) — Wrapper element — `'figcaption'` inside a `<figure>` quote card.
  - className?: string — Classes on the wrapping row (per-variant modifier rides here).
  - metaClassName?: string — Extra classes on the inner name/role column.
  - person: { name?: ReactNode; role?: ReactNode; avatar?: ReactNode; } — The attributee — structurally compatible with `Testimonial`.

Usage:
```tsx
<TestimonialFigure />
```

### InView
Import: `import { InView } from 'raditz'`

InView — a thin client wrapper that toggles a class on its element the first time it scrolls into view (via the shared {@link useInView} IntersectionObserver). The animation itself is pure CSS, keyed off that class; InView only supplies the in-view signal — so it composes with any class-driven scroll effect. SSR-safe: the class is added client-side, and Raditz's reveal CSS is gated on `@media (scripting: enabled)`, so server/no-JS renders the final visible state. Used by {@link SectionShell } for the section content choreography; reusable on its own.

Props:
  - as?: ElementType (default: div) — Element/tag to render.
  - inViewClassName?: string (default: is-in) — Class added the first time the element scrolls into view.
  - repeat?: boolean (default: false) — Re-toggle every time it re-enters view (default latches once).

Usage:
```tsx
<InView />
```

### HeroBleed
Import: `import { HeroBleed } from 'raditz'`

HeroBleed — a thin preset of {@link SectionShell}: one background fills the block (default a gradient) so it reaches the top BEHIND a transparent `nav` slot, with the hero content below. The bleed mechanism is decoupled from the content, so any hero design slots in. Media auto-scrims (and SectionShell then scopes the content to the on-dark context). It's a named preset, not its own Frame/SectionBackground/padding stack — that all lives in SectionShell.

Props:
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh" (default: gradient-aurora)
  - children?: ReactNode — The hero content — any design; the bleed mechanism is decoupled from it.
  - image?: string
  - nav?: ReactNode — A transparent nav rendered at the very top, floating over the shared background (pass a nav with no background of its own).
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken the backdrop for legible text. Defaults on when image/video is set.
  - video?: string
  - wrap?: string — Extra classes on the hero content's `.s-wrap`.

Usage:
```tsx
<HeroBleed>…</HeroBleed>
```

## media

### Carousel
Import: `import { Carousel } from 'raditz'`

Carousel — a horizontal scroll-snap slider. Each child is a slide. `perView` sets how many slides show at once (fractional peeks the next); omit it for a responsive default. Arrows + dots are built in; `autoplay` advances every `interval` ms and `loop` wraps. Touch/trackpad swipe works via native scroll-snap; programmatic paging is a token-timed smooth scroll (it honours the project motion scale and `prefers-reduced-motion`).

Props:
  - arrows?: boolean (default: true) — Show prev/next arrows.
  - autoplay?: boolean (default: false) — Auto-advance.
  - bleed?: boolean (default: false) — Let the track bleed past the section's horizontal padding so peeking slides reach the edges instead of being clipped by the gutter.
  - children?: ReactNode — Each child is a slide.
  - dots?: boolean (default: true) — Show dot indicators.
  - gap?: string (default: var(--space-4)) — Gap between slides (CSS length).
  - interval?: number (default: 4500) — Auto-advance interval in ms.
  - loop?: boolean (default: true) — Wrap past the ends.
  - perView?: number — Slides visible at once (fractional peeks the next). Omit for a responsive default: ~1.15 on small screens scaling up to ~2.5 on wide ones, so there's always more than one slide hinting at further content.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, SingleSlide

Usage:
```tsx
<Carousel>…</Carousel>
```

### Gallery
Import: `import { Gallery } from 'raditz'`

Gallery — a responsive thumbnail grid that opens a Lightbox on click. Pass the same `images` shape as Lightbox (`[{ src, thumb?, alt?, caption? }]`). `columns` sets the grid (it auto-collapses on small screens); `aspect` sets each cell's aspect-ratio (e.g. "1", "4/3", "3/4"), or "masonry" for natural heights.

Props:
  - aspect?: string (default: 1) — Cell aspect-ratio (e.g. "1", "4/3"), or "masonry" for natural heights.
  - columns?: number (default: 3) — Columns on wide screens (auto-collapses on small).
  - gap?: string (default: var(--space-3)) — Grid gap (CSS length).
  - images?: LightboxImage[] (default: [])

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Gallery />
```

### Marquee
Import: `import { Marquee } from 'raditz'`

Marquee — a seamless, infinitely-scrolling row of its children (logos, tags, quotes…). The content is duplicated so the loop has no seam. Pauses on hover and respects `prefers-reduced-motion` (animation stops, duplicate hidden, so it degrades to a static, readable row). All token-driven, so it re-themes.

Props:
  - direction?: "left" | "right" (default: left) — Scroll direction.
  - duration?: number (default: 26) — Seconds for one full loop.
  - fade?: boolean (default: true) — Fade the edges with a mask.
  - gap?: string (default: var(--space-7)) — Gap between items (CSS length).
  - pauseOnHover?: boolean (default: true) — Pause the scroll on hover.

Examples (Storybook stories): Logos, Reverse

Usage:
```tsx
<Marquee />
```

## motion

### AnimatedIcon
Import: `import { AnimatedIcon } from 'raditz'`

AnimatedIcon — wraps any icon in a tasteful idle animation: `float`, `orbit`, `pulse`, `spin`, `wiggle`, or a one-shot `draw` (stroked icons only, e.g. the Raditz `<Icon/>`). Built to pair with `react-icons` — it's icon-agnostic, only styling its child, so it ships dependency-free and tree-shakeable. Timing rides the shared motion tokens (re-tunes with `data-motion`) and it honours `prefers-reduced-motion` by rendering the icon static.

Props:
  - anim: "float" | "orbit" | "pulse" | "spin" | "wiggle" | "draw" — Which looping (or one-shot, for `draw`) animation to play.
  - children: ReactNode — The icon: a react-icons glyph (`<GiMoonOrbit/>`), a Raditz `<Icon/>`, or raw SVG.
  - paused?: boolean (default: false) — Freeze the animation (e.g. resume on hover via your own class).
  - speed?: "slow" | "base" | "fast" (default: base) — Speed bucket — multiplies the base duration.

Examples (Storybook stories): Gallery

Usage:
```tsx
<AnimatedIcon>…</AnimatedIcon>
```

### Reveal
Import: `import { Reveal } from 'raditz'`

Reveal — a tasteful, opt-in scroll entrance. Wraps any content; when it scrolls into view it transitions from a hidden state (fade / rise / scale / zoom / blur / slide / flip / rotate / skew) to its resting state, using the shared motion tokens for timing. Transform/opacity/filter only (no layout thrash); driven by one IntersectionObserver via {@link useInView }. With no `anim`, it inherits the app-wide reveal style (`data-reveal`). Honours `prefers-reduced-motion` — it then renders the final state immediately, never the hidden one.

Props:
  - anim?: "fade" | "rise" | "scale" | "fade-rise" | "zoom" | "blur" | "slide-left" | "slide-right" | "flip" | "flip-y" | "rotate" | "skew" — Entrance style. Omit to inherit the app-wide reveal style (`data-reveal` on `<html>`, set by the theme config); falls back to `fade-rise` when none is set.
  - as?: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements> (default: 'div') — Element/tag to render.
  - delay?: number (default: 0) — Extra delay (ms) on top of any group stagger.
  - index?: number (default: 0) — Stagger position — set automatically by {@link RevealGroup}.
  - repeat?: boolean (default: false) — Replay every time it re-enters view (default plays once).

Examples (Storybook stories): StaggeredGroup, EachAnim

Usage:
```tsx
<Reveal />
```

### RevealGroup
Import: `import { RevealGroup } from 'raditz'`

RevealGroup — staggers a set of {@link Reveal} children by auto-assigning each an `index`, so a grid/list cascades in. The stagger is pure CSS (a per-item `transition-delay`), so there are no JS timers.

Props:
  - anim?: "fade" | "rise" | "scale" | "fade-rise" | "zoom" | "blur" | "slide-left" | "slide-right" | "flip" | "flip-y" | "rotate" | "skew" — Default anim for child {@link Reveal}s that don't set their own.
  - as?: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements>
  - stagger?: number (default: 60) — Per-item stagger between children (ms).

Examples (Storybook stories): StaggeredGroup, EachAnim

Usage:
```tsx
<RevealGroup />
```

### TextReveal
Import: `import { TextReveal } from 'raditz'`

TextReveal — a kinetic headline: splits `text` into words (or chars) that cascade in on scroll with a per-unit `flip` / `rise` / `fade` / `blur` / `mask` entrance. A11y-safe (full text read once, fragments hidden — see {@link splitText}), transform/opacity/clip only, and honours `prefers-reduced-motion` (renders the plain string). Pair with a heading class (`h-display`/`h-section`) for a hero.

Props:
  - anim?: "mask" | "flip" | "rise" | "fade" | "blur" (default: flip) — Per-unit entrance.
  - as?: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements> (default: 'span') — Element/tag to render.
  - by?: "word" | "char" (default: word) — Split granularity.
  - repeat?: boolean (default: false) — Replay every time it re-enters view.
  - stagger?: number (default: 40) — Per-unit stagger (ms).
  - text: string — The text to animate — a plain string so it can split safely.

Examples (Storybook stories): PerAnim, PerChar

Usage:
```tsx
<TextReveal />
```

## navigation

### Breadcrumb
Import: `import { Breadcrumb } from 'raditz'`

Breadcrumb — hierarchical trail. `items` is `[{ label, href?, onClick? }]`; the last is the current page. Separators are chevrons by default (`separator` overrides).

Props:
  - items?: BreadcrumbItem[] (default: []) — Trail steps, root first; the last is the current page.
  - separator?: ReactNode — Separator between steps. Defaults to a chevron; pass e.g. "/" for a slash trail. Rendered aria-hidden either way.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Breadcrumb />
```

### NavBar
Import: `import { NavBar } from 'raditz'`

NavBar — a route nav with a single indicator that *flows* between items as the active one changes (measured from the live item rects, so it works at any width). `items` is `[{ key, label, icon?, href? }]`. Controlled with `active` / `onChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultActive`. `variant`: 'pill' (filled highlight that slides) or 'underline' (sliding bottom bar). `orientation` 'horizontal' | 'vertical'.

Props:
  - active?: string — Active item key (controlled).
  - defaultActive?: string — Initial active key (uncontrolled; defaults to the first item).
  - items?: NavBarItem[] (default: [])
  - onChange?: ((key: string) => void)
  - orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical" (default: horizontal)
  - variant?: "pill" | "underline" (default: pill) — Sliding highlight style.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<NavBar />
```

### NavigationMenu
Import: `import { NavigationMenu } from 'raditz'`

NavigationMenu — a horizontal site nav (Radix NavigationMenu). `items` is `[{ label, href?, content? }]`: entries with `content` open a dropdown panel on hover/focus; plain entries are links. Panels render through the shared Overlay, so they match the rest of the overlay system.

Props:
  - items?: NavigationMenuItem[] (default: [])

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<NavigationMenu />
```

### PageHeader
Import: `import { PageHeader } from 'raditz'`

PageHeader — the standard top-of-page block: optional breadcrumb, an eyebrow, a title, a description, and a right-aligned `actions` slot. Keeps every page's header consistent instead of re-laying-out each time.

Props:
  - actions?: ReactNode — Right-aligned actions (buttons, etc.).
  - breadcrumb?: ReactNode — Breadcrumb node placed above the title.
  - description?: ReactNode
  - eyebrow?: ReactNode
  - title?: ReactNode

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<PageHeader />
```

### Pagination
Import: `import { Pagination } from 'raditz'`

Pagination — page navigation with prev/next and an ellipsised page list. Controlled with `page` / `onChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultPage`. `siblings` controls how many pages show around the current one.

Props:
  - defaultPage?: number (default: 1) — Initial page (uncontrolled).
  - onChange?: ((page: number) => void)
  - page?: number — Current page, 1-based (controlled).
  - siblings?: number (default: 1) — Pages shown each side of the current one.
  - total?: number (default: 1) — Total number of pages.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Pagination />
```

### Stepper
Import: `import { Stepper } from 'raditz'`

Stepper — a horizontal (or vertical) progress indicator for multi-step flows. `steps` is `[{ label, description? }]`; `current` is the active 0-based index. Steps before `current` render complete (check), the rest upcoming. Clickable when `onStepClick` is provided.

Props:
  - current?: number (default: 0) — Active 0-based index.
  - onStepClick?: ((index: number) => void) — Makes completed/current steps clickable.
  - orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical" (default: horizontal)
  - steps?: StepperStep[] (default: [])

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Stepper />
```

### Tabs
Import: `import { Tabs } from 'raditz'`

A tab switcher. Pass `tabs` as { value, label } items. Controlled via `value` + `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`. `variant` is the segmented control (default) or an underline bar. Implements the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with automatic activation: the selected tab is the single tab stop and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End move focus AND selection together.

Props:
  - className?: string
  - defaultValue?: string — Initial value (uncontrolled).
  - onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Fires on tab change.
  - tabs?: TabItem[] (default: []) — Tab definitions.
  - value?: string — Controlled active value.
  - variant?: "segmented" | "underline" (default: segmented)

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Tabs />
```

### Toolbar
Import: `import { Toolbar } from 'raditz'`

Toolbar — a horizontal container that groups actions (Radix Toolbar). Put IconButtons, Buttons, Toggles and ToggleGroups inside; separate groups with `<Separator orientation="vertical" />`. The toolbar is a single tab stop: arrow keys (orientation from `aria-orientation`, horizontal by default) and Home/End move focus between the controls inside it. Composite children that handle their own arrow keys (e.g. a single-select ToggleGroup) call preventDefault, so the toolbar leaves those events alone.

Props:
  - as?: ElementType (default: div)

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Toolbar />
```

### Tree
Import: `import { Tree } from 'raditz'`

Tree — an accessible tree view (WAI-ARIA `tree` pattern) with a split row: clicking a row's NAME selects it (`onSelect` fires for leaves and branches), while the chevron toggles a branch open/closed without selecting. Selection and expansion are each controllable or uncontrolled. Full keyboard support: Up/Down move between visible rows, Right/Left expand/collapse (or step in/out), Enter/Space select, Home/End jump to ends. Roving tabindex keeps a single tab stop. `toggleOnRowClick` opts back into file-browser behaviour (row click also toggles).

Props:
  - defaultExpandedIds?: string[] — Initially expanded ids (uncontrolled).
  - defaultSelectedId?: string — Initial selected id (uncontrolled).
  - expandedIds?: string[] — Controlled set of expanded ids.
  - items: TreeNode[] — The node forest to render.
  - onExpandedChange?: ((ids: string[]) => void) — Fires when the expanded set changes.
  - onSelect?: ((id: string, node: TreeNode) => void) — Fires when a row is activated.
  - selectedId?: string — Controlled selected id.
  - toggleOnRowClick?: boolean (default: false) — Opt-in file-browser behaviour: clicking a folder row ALSO toggles it. By default the row (name) only selects — `onSelect` fires for leaves and branches alike — and expansion is the chevron's (and ←/→'s) job.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, Controlled

Usage:
```tsx
<Tree />
```

## overlay

### AlertDialog
Import: `import { AlertDialog } from 'raditz'`

AlertDialog — a modal confirmation (Radix AlertDialog). Like Dialog but requires an explicit choice: it does NOT close on scrim click (Escape cancels). `tone` colors the confirm action. An adapter face over {@link Overlay}: the "no outside-dismiss" behavior is one honest flag (`dismissOnOutside={false}`), not a ref-targeting trick.

Props:
  - actionText?: string (default: Confirm) — Confirm button label.
  - cancelText?: string (default: Cancel) — Cancel button label.
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled) — the dialog then owns open/close itself (Escape, cancel, confirm).
  - description?: ReactNode
  - onAction?: (() => void) — Fires when the confirm action is chosen (dialog then closes).
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void) — Fires to request open/close.
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled).
  - title?: ReactNode
  - tone?: "accent" | "danger" (default: danger) — Confirm-button tone.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<AlertDialog />
```

### BottomSheet
Import: `import { BottomSheet } from 'raditz'`

BottomSheet — a mobile-first sheet fixed to the viewport bottom (full width up to the container measure, top corners rounded, slides up). Controlled with `open` / `onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled via `defaultOpen`; render your own trigger. Closes on Escape, scrim click, the close button, or by dragging the grab handle / title bar down past a quarter of its height ({@link shouldCloseFromDrag}). Focus is trapped and body scroll locked while open. An adapter face over {@link Overlay} (`side: bottom` topology, focus trap). The drag offset travels as the `--rdz-sheet-drag` custom property (data, not inline styling) — the stylesheet turns it into the transform.

Props:
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled) — the sheet then owns open/close itself (Escape, scrim, close button, drag-to-close).
  - description?: ReactNode — Sub-heading / description text.
  - footer?: ReactNode — Footer node (usually action buttons).
  - height?: "auto" | "tall" (default: auto) — Sheet height: `auto` sizes to content (up to 90svh); `tall` is near-full, leaving the top safe-area clear.
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void) — Fires to request open/close.
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled).
  - title?: ReactNode — Heading text (title bar, like Dialog's).

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, Tall

Usage:
```tsx
<BottomSheet />
```

### shouldCloseFromDrag
Import: `import { shouldCloseFromDrag } from 'raditz'`

Drag-to-close decision: a release counts as "close" when the sheet was dragged down past 25% of its own height. Pure — unit-testable without a DOM. A zero/unmeasured height never closes (a phantom close on a sheet that hasn't laid out yet would eat the user's content).

Props: none

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, Tall

Usage:
```tsx
<shouldCloseFromDrag />
```

### CommandPalette
Import: `import { CommandPalette } from 'raditz'`

CommandPalette — a ⌘K / Ctrl-K command launcher. `groups` is `[{ heading, items: [{ id, label, icon?, shortcut?, keywords?, onSelect }] }]`. Controlled with `open` / `onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled via `defaultOpen`. With `hotkey` (default true) it binds ⌘K/Ctrl-K globally to toggle. Type to fuzzy-filter; Arrow/Enter run. An adapter face over {@link Overlay} (`centered` modal, focus trap).

Props:
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled) — the palette then owns open/close itself (hotkey, Escape, scrim, running a command).
  - groups?: CommandGroup[] (default: [])
  - hotkey?: boolean (default: true) — Bind ⌘K / Ctrl-K globally to toggle.
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void)
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled).
  - placeholder?: string (default: Type a command or search…)

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<CommandPalette />
```

### ContextMenu
Import: `import { ContextMenu } from 'raditz'`

ContextMenu — a right-click (desktop) / long-press (touch) menu over an area (Radix ContextMenu). Wrap the target; right-click or press-and-hold opens the same menu model as DropdownMenu at the pointer. Items: `{ label, icon?, shortcut?, onSelect?, disabled?, danger? }`, plus `{ separator: true }` and `{ heading: true, label }`. Open state may be controlled (`open` / `onOpenChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultOpen`), like its menu peers. An adapter face over {@link MenuSurface} (`point` topology) — so it shares keyboard roving with the other menus.

Props:
  - children?: ReactNode — The area that responds to right-click / long-press.
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled).
  - items?: MenuItem[] (default: []) — Menu rows — same model as DropdownMenu.
  - longPressMs?: number (default: 480) — Touch press-and-hold duration (ms) that opens the menu.
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void) — Fires to request open/close (right-click/long-press → true; select/dismiss → false).
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled). The menu opens at the last pointer position.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<ContextMenu>…</ContextMenu>
```

### Dialog
Import: `import { Dialog } from 'raditz'`

Dialog — a modal overlay (Radix Dialog). Controlled with `open` / `onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled via `defaultOpen`; render your own trigger. Closes on Escape, scrim click, or the close button. Focus is trapped while open and restored on close. An adapter face over {@link Overlay} (`centered` topology, focus trap).

Props:
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled) — the dialog then owns open/close itself (Escape, scrim, close button).
  - description?: ReactNode — Sub-heading / description text.
  - footer?: ReactNode — Footer node (usually action buttons).
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void) — Fires to request open/close.
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled).
  - size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default: md) — Panel width.
  - title?: ReactNode — Heading text.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Dialog />
```

### Drawer
Import: `import { Drawer } from 'raditz'`

Drawer — a panel that slides in from an edge (Radix-style sheet). Controlled with `open` / `onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled via `defaultOpen`. `side` picks the edge; `size` sets width (left/ right) or height (top/bottom). Closes on Escape, scrim click or the close button; focus is trapped and body scroll locked while open. An adapter face over {@link Overlay} (`side` topology, focus trap).

Props:
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled) — the drawer then owns open/close itself (Escape, scrim, close button).
  - description?: ReactNode
  - footer?: ReactNode
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void)
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled).
  - side?: "left" | "right" | "top" | "bottom" (default: right) — Edge it slides from.
  - size?: string (default: 22rem) — Width (left/right) or height (top/bottom).
  - title?: ReactNode

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, NoTitle

Usage:
```tsx
<Drawer />
```

### DropdownMenu
Import: `import { DropdownMenu } from 'raditz'`

DropdownMenu — a button-triggered menu (Radix DropdownMenu). Items are `{ label, icon?, shortcut?, onSelect?, disabled?, danger? }`, plus `{ separator: true }` and `{ heading: true, label }`. Arrow keys move focus, Enter selects, Escape closes. An adapter face: the trigger lives here; {@link MenuSurface} owns positioning, dismissal, roving, and item rendering.

Props:
  - align?: "start" | "center" | "end" (default: start) — Cross-axis alignment.
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false)
  - items?: MenuItem[] (default: []) — Menu rows — items, `{separator:true}`, or `{heading:true,label}`.
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void)
  - open?: boolean
  - side?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" (default: bottom) — Preferred side.
  - trigger?: ReactNode — Trigger element (click toggles the menu).

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<DropdownMenu />
```

### HoverCard
Import: `import { HoverCard } from 'raditz'`

HoverCard — preview content shown on hover/focus of a trigger (Radix HoverCard). Opens after `openDelay`, closes after `closeDelay`; staying over the card keeps it open. An adapter face over {@link Overlay} (`anchored` topology). HoverCard drives its own open state via hover timers, so it disables Overlay's dismissal.

Props:
  - align?: "start" | "center" | "end" (default: center) — Cross-axis alignment.
  - closeDelay?: number (default: 150) — Ms before closing.
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled).
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void)
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled).
  - openDelay?: number (default: 200) — Ms before opening.
  - side?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" (default: bottom) — Preferred side.
  - trigger?: ReactNode — Element that reveals the card on hover/focus.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<HoverCard />
```

### Lightbox
Import: `import { Lightbox } from 'raditz'`

Lightbox — a full-screen image viewer (gallery modal). Controlled with `open` + `index`, or uncontrolled with `defaultOpen` / `defaultIndex`. Arrow keys and the on-screen arrows page; the image follows your finger and slides on swipe. Zoom with a pinch (trackpad or touch), the +/− buttons, or a click; drag to pan when zoomed. Swipe down (or click the black space, or Escape) to close. Pan/zoom/swipe are driven imperatively (the transform is written straight to the image, not through React state) so a drag stays at the display's frame rate instead of thrashing a render per pointer move. The chrome always renders on a dark scrim (identical in light + dark themes) via `.rdz-on-dark`.

Props:
  - defaultIndex?: number (default: 0) — Initial index (uncontrolled).
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled).
  - filmstrip?: boolean (default: false) — Show the thumbnail filmstrip.
  - images?: LightboxImage[] (default: [])
  - index?: number — Active image index (controlled).
  - onIndexChange?: ((index: number) => void)
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void)
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled).

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Lightbox />
```

### Menubar
Import: `import { Menubar } from 'raditz'`

Menubar — a horizontal row of menus (Radix Menubar), like an app menu bar. `menus` is `[{ label, items }]` where `items` use the DropdownMenu model (`{ label, icon?, shortcut?, onSelect?, disabled?, danger? }`, `{ separator }`, `{ heading, label }`). Once a menu is open, hovering siblings switches to them, and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move between menus. Open state may be controlled (`open` / `onOpenChange`, the open menu's index) or uncontrolled (`defaultOpen`).

Props:
  - defaultOpen?: number (default: -1) — Initially open menu index (uncontrolled).
  - menus?: MenubarMenu[] (default: []) — Top-level menus, each with its own item list.
  - onOpenChange?: ((openIndex: number) => void) — Fires with the newly open menu's index (-1 when closing).
  - open?: number — Index of the open menu (controlled); -1 = all closed.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Menubar />
```

### Popover
Import: `import { Popover } from 'raditz'`

Popover — floating content anchored to a trigger (Radix Popover). Click the trigger to toggle; closes on Escape or outside click. Non-modal (focus is not trapped). `side`/`align` place the panel and flip near the viewport edge. An adapter face over {@link Overlay} (`anchored` topology, focus `none`). The trigger and its click-to-toggle stay here; Overlay owns the surface.

Props:
  - align?: "start" | "center" | "end" (default: center) — Cross-axis alignment.
  - defaultOpen?: boolean (default: false) — Initial open state (uncontrolled).
  - onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void)
  - open?: boolean — Open state (controlled).
  - side?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" (default: bottom) — Preferred side.
  - trigger?: ReactNode — Trigger element (click toggles the popover).

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Popover />
```

### Tooltip
Import: `import { Tooltip } from 'raditz'`

A hover/focus tooltip. Wraps a focusable trigger; `label` is the bubble. The bubble renders through the shared {@link Overlay} machinery — portaled to <body> and collision-positioned (flips + clamps to the viewport), so it never runs off-screen the way the old pure-CSS bubble did. The trigger must be focusable (a button/link) so keyboard users get the tooltip too.

Props:
  - align?: "center" | "start" | "end" (default: center) — Cross-axis alignment of the bubble vs. the trigger.
  - delay?: number (default: 200) — Open delay on hover/focus (ms).
  - label: ReactNode — Bubble content.
  - side?: "top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right" (default: top) — Side of the trigger the bubble opens on; flips to the opposite side on overflow.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Tooltip />
```

### AnimationsA
Import: `import { AnimationsA } from 'raditz'`

Animations A — scroll-reveal entrances (every variant), with a Replay control.

Props:
  - animate?: boolean | "scroll" | "load" (default: 'scroll') — Content entrance choreography, forwarded to {@link SectionShell}: `'scroll'` (default) reveals on scroll, `'load'` animates on mount (above-the-fold heroes), `false` is static.
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh" (default: none)
  - children?: ReactNode — Replaces the auto-rendered body inside the themed shell when provided.
  - className?: string — Consumer class merged onto the section's root element.
  - heading?: ReactNode (default: Scroll-reveal entrances) — Section heading.
  - id?: string — Anchor id on the section's root element (in-page nav targets).
  - image?: string
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - video?: string

Examples (Storybook stories): A_ScrollReveal, B_TitleAndText, C_IconMotion, D_PresetCards

Usage:
```tsx
<AnimationsA>…</AnimationsA>
```

### ContactA
Import: `import { ContactA } from 'raditz'`

Contact A — split contact section: intro column (header, lede, labelled details, optional aside) beside a message form. The default form is uncontrolled name/email/message (name + email required) with a submit button; pass `form` to swap in your own, or `children` to replace the whole body.

Props:
  - align?: "start" | "center" (default: start) — Header alignment. Defaults to 'start' so the heading shares the intro column's left edge beside the form.
  - animate?: boolean | "scroll" | "load" (default: 'scroll') — Content entrance choreography, forwarded to {@link SectionShell}: `'scroll'` (default) reveals on scroll, `'load'` animates on mount (above-the-fold heroes), `false` is static.
  - aside?: ReactNode — Extra node pinned under the details (e.g. opening hours, a map embed).
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh"
  - children?: ReactNode — Replaces the auto-rendered body inside the themed shell when provided.
  - className?: string — Consumer class merged onto the section's root element.
  - details?: ContactDetail[] — Labelled contact details (email, phone, address…) under the lede.
  - eyebrow?: ReactNode
  - form?: ReactNode — Replaces the default name/email/message form entirely.
  - heading?: ReactNode
  - id?: string — Anchor id on the section's root element (in-page nav targets).
  - image?: string
  - lede?: ReactNode — Intro paragraph under the header.
  - onSubmit?: ((values: ContactValues) => void) — Receives the typed values on submit. The default is prevented and the values are read from `FormData` — the inputs stay uncontrolled.
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - submitLabel?: string (default: Send message) — Submit button label on the default form.
  - video?: string

Examples (Storybook stories): A_Split, WithAside, CustomForm

Usage:
```tsx
<ContactA>…</ContactA>
```

  - className?: string — Consumer class merged onto the section's root element.
  - heading?: ReactNode — Optional section heading rendered above the content.
  - id?: string — Anchor id on the section's root element (in-page nav targets).
  - image?: string
  - items: { question: ReactNode; answer: ReactNode; }[] — FAQ items (required).
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - video?: string

Examples (Storybook stories): A_Accordion, A_CenteredHeading, B_TwoColumn

Usage:
```tsx
<FaqA>…</FaqA>
```

### FeaturesTabbed
Import: `import { FeaturesTabbed } from 'raditz'`

FeaturesTabbed — a vertical tab rail beside a detail panel: pick an offering on the left, read its lead (price/rates), description, ticked feature list and CTA on the right. Built for "a few rich, comparable offerings" where cards bury the detail. The panel holds a steady min-height so switching tabs never makes the page jump. Uncontrolled (first tab open) — a deep section, no wiring required.

Props:
  - align?: "start" | "center" (default: start) — Header alignment. Defaults to 'start' so the heading shares the rail's left edge — a centered heading floats awkwardly over the asymmetric rail + panel grid.
  - animate?: boolean | "scroll" | "load" (default: 'scroll') — Content entrance choreography, forwarded to {@link SectionShell}: `'scroll'` (default) reveals on scroll, `'load'` animates on mount (above-the-fold heroes), `false` is static.
  - aside?: ReactNode — Extra node pinned under the tab rail (e.g. opening hours, terms).
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh"
  - children?: ReactNode — Replaces the auto-rendered body inside the themed shell when provided.
  - className?: string — Consumer class merged onto the section's root element.
  - eyebrow?: ReactNode
  - heading?: ReactNode
  - id?: string — Anchor id on the section's root element (in-page nav targets).
  - image?: string
  - items: FeaturesTabbedItem[] — One entry per tab (required).
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - video?: string

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<FeaturesTabbed>…</FeaturesTabbed>
```

### GalleryA
Import: `import { GalleryA } from 'raditz'`

Gallery A — header + lightbox grid. Composes the media {@link GalleryGrid} component (grid + Lightbox), forwarding `columns`/`aspect` — no duplicate grid/lightbox machinery here.

Props:
  - align?: "start" | "center" (default: 'start') — Align the header block: 'center' or 'start' (left).
  - animate?: boolean | "scroll" | "load" (default: 'scroll') — Content entrance choreography, forwarded to {@link SectionShell}: `'scroll'` (default) reveals on scroll, `'load'` animates on mount (above-the-fold heroes), `false` is static.
  - aspect?: string (default: "1") — Cell aspect-ratio, forwarded to the media Gallery (GalleryA only).
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh" (default: none)
  - children?: ReactNode — Replaces the auto-rendered body inside the themed shell when provided.
  - className?: string — Consumer class merged onto the section's root element.
  - columns?: number (default: 3) — Grid columns, forwarded to the media Gallery (GalleryA only).
  - eyebrow?: ReactNode — Kicker line above the heading.
  - heading?: ReactNode — Section heading.
  - id?: string — Anchor id on the section's root element (in-page nav targets).
  - image?: string
  - images: { src: string; alt: string; caption?: ReactNode; }[] — Images to render (required). `alt` is mandatory — gallery imagery is content, not decoration. `caption` shows under each figure in GalleryB (and in the GalleryA lightbox viewer).
  - lede?: ReactNode — Supporting line under the heading.
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - video?: string

Examples (Storybook stories): A_LightboxGrid, B_Masonry

Usage:
```tsx
<GalleryA>…</GalleryA>
```

### HeroA
Import: `import { HeroA } from 'raditz'`

Hero A — centered column, dual CTA. Heroes are above the fold, so they default to the `'load'` entrance — a pure-CSS mount animation that plays at first paint (no observer, no blank flash). Pass `animate="scroll"` to reveal on scroll instead, or `false` for static.

  - image?: string
  - lede?: ReactNode — Lead paragraph under the title.
  - media?: ReactNode — Media slot (used by the split/full-bleed variants).
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - title: ReactNode — Headline (required).
  - video?: string

### ImageFocus
Import: `import { ImageFocus } from 'raditz'`

ImageFocus — a full-bleed image section with optional text over it. The one component for both a media **hero** (with the page's nav bleeding over it) AND an **inline** image band that gives a page some visual breathing room (image alone, or image + a line of copy). The image always covers; the text block's `align` (left/centre), `place` (centre/bottom) and `titleSize` are configurable so the same component reads as a punchy hero or a quiet inline band.

Props:
  - actions?: SectionAction[] — CTAs.
  - align?: "start" | "center" (default: center) — Horizontal alignment of the text block.
  - animate?: boolean | "scroll" | "load" (default: 'scroll') — Content entrance choreography, forwarded to {@link SectionShell}: `'scroll'` (default) reveals on scroll, `'load'` animates on mount (above-the-fold heroes), `false` is static.
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh"
  - children?: ReactNode — Replaces the auto-rendered body inside the themed shell when provided.
  - className?: string — Consumer class merged onto the section's root element.
  - eyebrow?: ReactNode — Eyebrow / kicker above the title.
  - id?: string — Anchor id on the section's root element (in-page nav targets).
  - image: string — Full-bleed background image URL (required).
  - parallax?: boolean
  - place?: "center" | "bottom" (default: center) — Vertical placement of the text.
  - scrim?: boolean (default: true) — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - size?: "hero" | "band" | "auto" (default: band) — Band height: a tall 'hero', a medium 'band', or 'auto' (fits content).
  - sub?: ReactNode — Sub-text under the title.
  - title?: ReactNode — Headline.
  - titleSize?: "section" | "display" (default: section) — Title visual size.
  - video?: string

Examples (Storybook stories): A_Hero, B_Band, C_ImageOnly

Usage:
```tsx
<ImageFocus>…</ImageFocus>
```

### NavbarA
Import: `import { NavbarA } from 'raditz'`

NavbarA — the default top nav: a compact, floating **glass pill** that re-themes with the accent. A preset over `NavCore` with the animated route-aware active indicator and a built-in light/dark toggle switched on. Collapses links into a burger sheet on narrow widths. `activeHref` overrides route auto-detection.

Props:
  - actions?: SectionAction[] — Call-to-action buttons.
  - activeHref?: string
  - animate?: boolean | "scroll" | "load" (default: 'scroll') — Content entrance choreography, forwarded to {@link SectionShell}: `'scroll'` (default) reveals on scroll, `'load'` animates on mount (above-the-fold heroes), `false` is static.
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh"
  - brand: NavbarBrand — Brand lockup (required).
  - children?: ReactNode — Replaces the auto-rendered body inside the themed shell when provided.
  - className?: string — Consumer class merged onto the section's root element.
  - id?: string — Anchor id on the section's root element (in-page nav targets).
  - image?: string
  - links?: NavbarLink[] — Primary nav links.
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - video?: string

Examples (Storybook stories): A_LogoLinksCTAs, A_NoLogoFallback, B_GlassCentered, C_MobileDropdown, D_BottomTabBar

Usage:
```tsx
<NavbarA>…</NavbarA>
```

### StorySplitA
Import: `import { StorySplitA } from 'raditz'`

StorySplit A — alternating editorial rows: each pairs a media pane (an image that covers, or a custom `media` node) with an eyebrow + title + body + CTA copy column. DOM order stays media → copy (reading order) on every row; even rows flip the media to the right purely presentationally via a `data-flip` attribute the stylesheet turns into grid `order` — and the flip resets when the rows stack on narrow containers, so media always sits above its copy.

Props:
  - align?: "start" | "center" — Align the heading block: 'center' or 'start' (left). Omit for the default look.
  - animate?: boolean | "scroll" | "load" (default: 'scroll') — Content entrance choreography, forwarded to {@link SectionShell}: `'scroll'` (default) reveals on scroll, `'load'` animates on mount (above-the-fold heroes), `false` is static.
  - background?: "none" | "surface" | "surface-2" | "gradient-accent" | "gradient-aurora" | "gradient-dusk" | "gradient-mesh"
  - children?: ReactNode — Replaces the auto-rendered body inside the themed shell when provided.
  - className?: string — Consumer class merged onto the section's root element.
  - eyebrow?: ReactNode — Small label above the section heading.
  - heading?: ReactNode — Section heading.
  - id?: string — Anchor id on the section's root element (in-page nav targets).
  - image?: string
  - items: StorySplitItem[] — Editorial rows to render (required).
  - parallax?: boolean
  - scrim?: boolean — Darken an `image`/`video`/gradient backdrop so overlaid text stays legible (and content switches to on-dark tokens). Essential when using `image` as a full-bleed section background behind copy.
  - video?: string

Examples (Storybook stories): A_Alternating, B_SingleRow, C_MediaNode

Usage:
```tsx
<StorySplitA>…</StorySplitA>
```

## surfaces

### Avatar
Import: `import { Avatar } from 'raditz'`

A user / brand avatar. Pass `src` for an image, or `initials` for a tinted monogram. `variant="orb"` renders the accent gradient sphere; combine it with `initials` for a monogram set into the orb surface.

Props:
  - alt?: string
  - initials?: string — Monogram fallback when there's no image.
  - size?: number | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" (default: md)
  - src?: string — Image source.
  - variant?: "solid" | "orb" (default: solid) — "orb" renders the accent gradient sphere.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, Orb, OrbInitials, Sizes

Usage:
```tsx
<Avatar />
```

### AvatarGroup
Import: `import { AvatarGroup } from 'raditz'`

AvatarGroup — overlapping avatars with a "+N" overflow chip. `items` is `[{ initials?, src?, alt?, name?, role?, href? }]`; `max` caps how many show before collapsing. Items with profile info reveal a hover card (and link out when given an `href`); the "+N" chip — always stacked on top — opens a popover listing everyone.

Props:
  - items?: AvatarGroupItem[] (default: [])
  - max?: number (default: 4) — Max avatars before collapsing to "+N".
  - size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (default: md)

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<AvatarGroup />
```

### Callout
Import: `import { Callout } from 'raditz'`

A bordered, tinted message panel for inline notices. `color` sets the tone; pass an `icon` element and optional `title`.

Props:
  - color?: "accent" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" (default: info) — Tone — every StatusTone except `neutral`.
  - icon?: ReactNode — Leading icon element.
  - title?: ReactNode — Optional bold title line.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, Tones

Usage:
```tsx
<Callout />
```

### Card
Import: `import { Card } from 'raditz'`

The base surface. `variant` is "solid" (default), "glass" (frosted blur) or "flat" (no shadow). `tone` paints a brand-colored treatment (accent / secondary / aurora / dusk / glass / mono) and sets the ink/arrow pairing for any `.rdz-card__*` children. `interactive` adds a hover lift for clickable cards.

Props:
  - as?: ElementType (default: div)
  - href?: string — Anchor attrs for a clickable card (`as="a"`).
  - interactive?: boolean (default: false) — Add a hover lift for clickable cards.
  - rel?: string
  - target?: string
  - tone?: "glass" | "accent" | "secondary" | "aurora" | "dusk" | "mono" — Brand-colored treatment — a soft accent / secondary / mono / gradient tint with matched ink + arrow colors.
  - variant?: "solid" | "glass" | "flat" (default: solid) — Surface style.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Card />
```

### CardArrow
Import: `import { CardArrow } from 'raditz'`

CardArrow — the consistent "this card is clickable" affordance. A horizontal right arrow for in-site links, or an up-right diagonal arrow for external ones. It gives a subtle nudge in its own direction when the host is hovered or keyboard-focused (add `rdz-card-arrow-host` to the clickable wrapper). Decorative, so it's `aria-hidden`.

Props:
  - external?: boolean (default: false) — External link (opens a new tab/window) → a diagonal up-right arrow; otherwise a horizontal right arrow for in-site navigation.

Examples (Storybook stories): InternalAndExternal

Usage:
```tsx
<CardArrow />
```

### EmptyState
Import: `import { EmptyState } from 'raditz'`

EmptyState — one component for the empty / loading / error placeholder patterns. Pass `icon` + `title` + `description` (+ optional `action`) for an empty state; set `loading` to swap the icon for a Spinner; use `tone="danger"` (with `icon="alert-triangle"`) for an error state.

Props:
  - action?: ReactNode
  - description?: ReactNode
  - icon?: enum
  - loading?: boolean (default: false) — Show a Spinner instead of the icon (loading state).
  - title?: ReactNode
  - tone?: "default" | "accent" | "danger" (default: default)

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<EmptyState />
```

### Vignette
Import: `import { Vignette } from 'raditz'`

Vignette — a styled visual area that plays its `scene` ONCE when it scrolls into view, and again whenever `replay` changes (a host card bumps it on hover). It never loops: the scene is remounted via a `key` so its one-shot CSS animation restarts. The Vignette owns the `prefers-reduced-motion` off-switch for its scene, and scenes time their CSS with the motion tokens — so the animation stays tied to the global system while the scene CONTENT is bespoke to each card. The `bg` is a preset, token-driven background treatment.

Props:
  - bg?: "plain" | "gradient" | "accent" | "secondary" | "mono" | "aurora" (default: gradient) — Background treatment, from the system palette.
  - replay?: number (default: 0) — Bump this number to replay the scene (the host card raises it on hover).
  - scene: ReactNode — The animated scene — a BESPOKE SVG / illustration authored for THIS card's subject (don't reuse one scene across cards). Its CSS animations should be ONE-SHOT (`animation-iteration-count: 1`) and timed with the motion tokens (`var(--duration-*)`, `var(--ease-*)`) so they ride `data-motion` and match the system's feel. They restart whenever the scene is (re)mounted — how reveal/hover replay works. Reduced motion is handled by the Vignette; the scene needs no off-switch.

Examples (Storybook stories): Backgrounds

Usage:
```tsx
<Vignette />
```

## typography

### CheckList
Import: `import { CheckList } from 'raditz'`

CheckList — a ticked feature list. The recurring "what's included" pattern: a list of points, each led by an accent check (or dot), optionally in two columns. A deep module so products stop hand-rolling `ul + icon + grid` CSS.

Props:
  - columns?: 1 | 2 (default: 1) — Lay out across this many columns (collapses to 1 on a narrow container).
  - items: ReactNode[] — The items to list (strings or nodes).
  - marker?: "check" | "dot" (default: check) — Marker style.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, TwoColumn, DotMarker

Usage:
```tsx
<CheckList />
```

### Code
Import: `import { Code } from 'raditz'`

Monospace code. Inline by default; pass `block` for a dark code block.

Props:
  - block?: boolean (default: false) — Render a dark block instead of inline code.

Examples (Storybook stories): Inline, Block

Usage:
```tsx
<Code />
```

### Eyebrow
Import: `import { Eyebrow } from 'raditz'`

The mono, upper-tracked label that sits above headings. Optional accent dot.

Props:
  - as?: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements> (default: span)
  - withDot?: boolean (default: false) — Show a leading accent dot.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, WithDot

Usage:
```tsx
<Eyebrow />
```

### Heading
Import: `import { Heading } from 'raditz'`

Section / page heading in the display typeface. `level` picks both the tag (h1–h4) and the size; override the visual size with `size` (e.g. an h2 that looks like display). `accent` colors a trailing period — the house flourish.

Props:
  - as?: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements>
  - level?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 (default: 2) — Tag + size: 1–4, or a display size.
  - size?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | "display" | "display-2xl" — Override the visual size independent of the tag.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, Scale

Usage:
```tsx
<Heading />
```

### Kbd
Import: `import { Kbd } from 'raditz'`

A keyboard key cap (⌘, Esc, ↵). Render one per key.

Props: none

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, Combination

Usage:
```tsx
<Kbd />
```

### Label
Import: `import { Label } from 'raditz'`

Label — a form label (Radix Label). Associate it with a control via `htmlFor`; `required` appends a danger-colored asterisk.

Props:
  - disabled?: boolean (default: false) — Dim the label to indicate its control is disabled.
  - htmlFor?: string — Id of the control this labels.
  - required?: boolean (default: false) — Append a required asterisk.

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<Label />
```

### Prose
Import: `import { Prose } from 'raditz'`

Prose — a long-form typography scope for rendered rich text (Markdown/MDX/CMS HTML) that you don't control element-by-element. Wrap the content and its descendant headings, paragraphs, lists, links, quotes, code, tables, images and rules pick up token-driven rhythm and spacing — no per-element classes. `measure` clamps the column to a readable length; `size` bumps the body scale.

Props:
  - as?: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements> (default: div) — Element to render.
  - measure?: boolean (default: true) — Clamp to a readable line length.
  - size?: "base" | "lg" (default: base) — Body type scale.

Examples (Storybook stories): Article, Large

Usage:
```tsx
<Prose />
```

### Text
Import: `import { Text } from 'raditz'`

Body copy. `as="p"` for paragraphs (default), `as="span"` for inline. `size` and `tone` map to the type + ink scales; `measure` clamps line length for long-form prose. Size/tone/weight are data-attributes styled in Text.scss.

Props:
  - as?: ElementType<any, keyof IntrinsicElements> (default: p)
  - measure?: boolean (default: false) — Clamp to a readable measure for long-form prose.
  - size?: "base" | "caption" | "s" | "l" (default: base) — Type size.
  - tone?: "default" | "soft" | "muted" | "faint" | "accent" (default: soft) — Ink level.
  - weight?: "regular" | "medium" | "semibold" | "bold" — Font weight token (regular|medium|semibold|bold).

Examples (Storybook stories): Default, Sizes, Tones

Usage:
```tsx
<Text />
```

### VisuallyHidden
Import: `import { VisuallyHidden } from 'raditz'`

VisuallyHidden — hides content visually while keeping it for screen readers (Radix VisuallyHidden).

Props:
  - as?: ElementType (default: span)

Examples (Storybook stories): Default

Usage:
```tsx
<VisuallyHidden />
```
